group.label: Measurement
group.comment: Times the observers on the guarded events, plus totals collection, product saves and queue consumers. Measurement on its own changes nothing about what runs — see Enforcement for that. Reports go to var/log/commerce/process_guard.log.

group.label: Enforcement
group.comment: These settings change what runs in production. Run bin/magento commerce:process-guard:policies first: it lists every observer on every guarded event, so a decision here is taken against evidence rather than a guess about which listener matters.

field.label: Never Run These Observers
field.comment: Comma-separated observer names from events.xml, or observer class names — either works, because whoever is reading a stack trace has the class and whoever is reading configuration has the name. This is the incident switch: it overrides everything else, including anything declared in code.

field.label: Advisory Observers
field.comment: Declared non-essential: a failure is logged instead of thrown, and they are skipped when their event is over budget and shedding is on. Only put an observer here if you would not fail an order over it.

field.label: Critical Observers
field.comment: Never contained, never skipped, whatever else is configured. Adding a name here can only make the guard do less, so it is always the safe direction.

field.label: Skip Advisory Observers Over Budget
field.comment: With this off, an advisory observer's failure is still contained but it always runs. Note what this cannot do: PHP has no way to interrupt work already in progress, so a budget is enforced between observers and never inside one. It stops a bad path getting worse; it does not make a slow observer fast.

field.label: Log A Summary Per Process
field.comment: Off by default. Breaches are always logged; summaries are every process every time, which is most of the volume. Useful while you are calibrating budgets on staging, noisy in production.
